result.title: Putting Transformer Theories to the Test
result.summary: Several formal theories have been developed to characterize the capabilities and limitations of the transformer architecture, each employing different abstractions that capture different features of the architecture. Due to the differences in their underlying assumptions and conceptual frameworks, these theories can disagree in their predictions about what tasks transformers find easy or hard. We map out seven theories of transformer capability (Star-free, $\mathsf{AC}^0$, $\mathsf{TC}^0$, C-RASP, MPC, BAPO, and Sensitivity) and translate their results into a common matrix of predictions across a suite of tasks covering different computational structures. We provide new theoretical results to complete this matrix. We then evaluate theoretical predictions through controlled experiments measuring in-distribution sample complexity, length generalization, and pretrained language model performance. We find that no single theory explains the observed pattern of successes and failures. When a theory does not capture the transformer behaviors relevant to a task, its predictions break down; for instance, we show that the $k$-hop induction task is predicted hard by C-RASP because it does not model content-dependent attention, but we train small transformers on this task that length-generalize. Similarly, theories assuming hard attention like $\mathsf{AC}^0$ and BAPO predict binary majority to be hard, for which we also find success in practice. Together, our results point to several specific features that a theory of transformers must capture: soft rather than hard attention, dynamic content-dependent retrieval, bounded computation at each position, an account of learnability and inductive biases, and a combination of upper and lower bounds.

AI.brief_summary: 将 Star-free、AC⁰、TC⁰、C-RASP、MPC、BAPO、Sensitivity 七种 Transformer 能力理论对齐到统一的任务预测矩阵，并用受控实验考察分布内样本复杂度、长度泛化与预训练语言模型表现是否与理论预测一致。
AI.relevance_reason: 论文指出的软注意力、内容依赖检索、逐位置有界计算与长度泛化实验范式，可供核查 LVR/VLM 中长度泛化与视觉证据检索的理论预测；但其对象为纯文本 Transformer 能力理论，未见视觉或 latent 推理实验，迁移线索需人工核查。
